trace_name: Carpal tunnel release: completeness never confirmed - persistent symptoms

errors.detail: release completed without confirming its completeness (m6.2 not performed); the most common reason for persistent symptoms after carpal tunnel release is incomplete release of the transverse carpal ligament, distally at the palmar arch or proximally at the antebrachial fascia (T27)

complications.detail: persistent symptoms declared as a postoperative consequence of the unconfirmed (incomplete) release (structural outcome; no physiology representation of entrapment exists in the engine, so no volume effect is computed)

description: [t=60s] m0.1: Review the referral, the electrodiagnostic confirmation and the symptom pattern; confirm the diagnosis of carpal tunnel syndrome and the indication for release
[t=120s] m0.2: Confirm consent and operative plan, including anticipation of median nerve variant anatomy (Lanz groups I-IV) and the possibility of nerve injury and repair
[t=180s] m0.3: Confirm team, resource tier and equipment plan for the case

[t=240s] m0.4: Establish anaesthesia: local anaesthetic alone is supported by strong evidence for this operation (T28); intravenous regional or general anaesthesia per patient factors and surgeon preference (T21)
[t=300s] m0.5: Apply the upper-arm tourniquet for a bloodless, visualised field

[t=360s] m0.6: Position the patient supine with the hand on a hand table, palm up; mark the surface landmarks - Kaplan's cardinal line distally, the hook of the hamate medially, the distal wrist crease proximally
[t=420s] m0.7: WHO Sign In completed before induction of anaesthesia

[t=480s] m0.8: Confirm that antibiotic prophylaxis is withheld: routine prophylaxis is not indicated for clean elective carpal tunnel release (T26; T28, limited evidence) - the withholding is a recorded decision, not an omission
[t=540s] m0.9: WHO Time Out completed immediately before skin incision

[t=600s] m1.1: Make the longitudinal skin incision on the ulnar aspect of the tunnel: from Kaplan's cardinal line distally toward the distal wrist crease proximally, along the axis of the radial border of the ring finger, 3-5 mm ulnar to the thenar crease, approximately 3-4 cm, not crossing the wrist crease
[t=660s] m1.2: Dissect through the subcutaneous fat under direct vision, identifying and preserving the cutaneous sensory branches crossing the field
[t=720s] m2.1: Divide the palmar fascia in line with its longitudinal fibres for the full length of the incision and expose the transverse carpal ligament along the whole field
[t=780s] m2.2: Review the operative findings at the wrist and confirm the plan to proceed with open release
[t=840s] dp1 -> proceed-open
[t=900s] m3.1: Release the antebrachial fascia proximally, on the ulnar side of the palmaris longus tendon and under direct vision, protecting the palmar cutaneous branch
[t=960s] m3.2: Make the small initial opening in the ligament at its proximal edge and identify the median nerve through it, at the proximal aspect of the wound
[t=1020s] m4.1: Demonstrate the median nerve identified at the proximal edge of the retinaculum and protected - looped and retracted clear of the division line

[t=1080s] m4.2: Establish the division limits: distally the superficial palmar arch beyond the volar fat pad (typically 18 mm beyond the ligament's distal edge); medially the ulnar neurovascular bundle at Guyon's canal, radial to the hook of the hamate

[t=1140s] m5.1: Account for the recurrent motor branch: state its expected course (Lanz group I) and set the division line on the ulnar side of the ligament, directed toward the ring finger, away from the branch
[t=1140s] Structures at risk identified and protected before division of the transverse carpal ligament achieved: all three criteria demonstrated
[t=1200s] m5.2: Confirm the ligament is clearly visible and fully exposed along the intended division line
[t=1260s] m5.3: Second look: re-confirm the identified nerve, the branch account and the division limits immediately before the pause
[t=1320s] m5.4: Pre-division pause: the identified nerve, the branch account and the division limits are verbalised and confirmed with the team before the ligament is divided
[t=1380s] m6.1: Divide the transverse carpal ligament longitudinally along its ulnar aspect, under direct vision, from the proximal opening to the volar fat pad - and no further
[t=1440s] m6.3: Inspect the tunnel and the nerve: no tumour, aberrant muscle or thickened synovium; the nerve's appearance recorded
[t=1500s] m7.1: Deflate the tourniquet, achieve haemostasis and inspect the wound
[t=1560s] m7.2: Re-inspect the median nerve and the thenar branch region at the end of the release: nerve integrity confirmed before closure
[t=1620s] m8.1: Close the skin (the ligament is left open - that is the release)
[t=1680s] m8.2: Confirm the postoperative plan: analgesia, elevation and early mobilisation; no routine supervised therapy and no prophylactic antibiotics (T28)
[t=1740s] m8.3: WHO Sign Out completed before the patient leaves the operating room
[t=1800s] complication recognised: incomplete-release
[t=1860s] dp4 -> return-theatre
plus: The structures at risk were identified and protected before the ligament was divided — median nerve demonstrated and protected, recurrent branch accounted for, division limits established (T21, T22).
Pre-division pause performed and the identification confirmed with the team before division (module safety culture, T20).
All three WHO checklist phases were completed at their integration points (T6).
delta: err.incomplete-release — release completed without confirming its completeness (m6.2 not performed); the most common reason for persistent symptoms after carpal tunnel release is incomplete release of the transverse carpal ligament, distally at the palmar arch or proximally at the antebrachial fascia (T27)
directive: Confirm the release before closing: the elevator must pass freely on both sides of the nerve and the fascia release must be confirmed — an unconfirmed release is the most common cause of persistent symptoms after this operation (T27; the completeness check, T21).
summary: Verdict: PASS (formative only — no construct evidence exists for these scores yet).
Checklist 96.6% (28/29), safety gate 4/4, process 4/5, physiology 7/7, management 5/5.

Next focus: err.incomplete-release — release completed without confirming its completeness (m6.2 not performed); the most common reason for persistent symptoms after carpal tunnel release is incomplete release of the transverse carpal ligament, distally at the palmar arch or proximally at the antebrachial fascia (T27)
